summary: Interleaved chat+embedding affinity mismatch causes intermittent tenant fallback and mixed responses
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reported interleaved user sessions where chat generation calls returned outputs from the canary variant while embedding calls for the same session were still pinned to the stable variant. This led to semantic mismatch (embeddings from v-stable but generated text from v-canary) causing downstream scoring failures and data skew.

Impact: Affects ~3% of requests for the BrightDocs tenant since rollout began; causes elevated error rates in their downstream similarity service and increased support tickets. Customer-facing incidents: search relevance dropped for certain cohorts.

Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east (tenant-dedicated-42) running a weighted canary (10% traffic) for redwood/gptx-13b-quant-v2. Embedding service rolled as a separate route to redwood/embed-1 pinned to v-stable by customer config.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer opens a chat flow that calls /v1/chat.generate then calls /v1/embeddings.create immediately after.
2) Repeat for a user with session cookies and an affinity token present.
3) In ~3% of attempts, chat.generate returned responses traced to canary hash and embeddings.create returned the stable model outputs.

Logs/observations:
- Edge request traces show identical session-affinity tokens attached to both requests.
- Routing decision logs show chat.generate went through route/variant: gptx-13b-quant-v2@canary-2026-03-09 while embeddings.create resolved to embed-1@stable-2026-02-21.
- Canary coordinator logs show an in-flight promote commit for the chat route at 2026-03-10T14:23:11Z overlapping with prewarm health probes for the embedding route that scheduled cache rewrites at 14:23:12Z.
- No obvious auth header mutation at the proxy level; however sidecar telemetry shows duplicate health probe responses for some edge nodes.

Initial hypothesis: An interleaving between the canary promote window and route-specific cache prewarm/healthprobe processing caused the routing table to transiently accept variant metadata for one service call but not the other for the same session token. This produced mixed-variant servicing within a single logical user transaction.
comments: Support (Alex Chen) 2026-03-10: Ingested customer report and validated traces. Customer provided three example trace IDs and timestamp ranges. Opened initial triage in #support-ops and requested SRE help.
SRE (Samir Patel) 2026-03-10: Noted overlapping timestamps of canary commit and prewarm. Requested edge logs and coordinator timeline. Assigned to Priya for routing deep-dive.

Engineering (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Reproduced routing discrepancy in internal test with synthetic affinity tokens by speeding up canary commit window; observed same mixed-resolution when prewarm cache rewrite collides with commit ack path. Created reproducer script and recorded deterministic failure at ~1:100 run rate in the test harness.

Customer (BrightDocs - Evan Morales) 2026-03-11: Confirmed that the reproducer mirrors production behavior. Provided additional batch of user traces and timeline for their scheduled traffic surge (2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11).

Support (Alex Chen) 2026-03-12: Coordinated temporary mitigation: recommend customer pin both chat and embedding routes explicitly to the same variant until rollback/patch is deployed. Customer applied pin to embed route; observed immediate reduction in mismatch reports.

Engineering (Priya Nair) 2026-03-12: Drafted a fix to the coordinator commit path to make route updates atomic across co-located route-sets and to add a short quiesce window to prewarm operations. Posting PR to edge-proxy and canary-coordinator. See related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4392.
investigation_notes: Reproducer: deterministic when promoting with artificial 50ms delay in commit-ack path and simultaneous prewarm cache writes—causes route metadata divergence for calls that happen within the window.

Root cause: coordinator promoted chat route variant and broadcasted route-change event; some edge nodes applied new variant metadata immediately while embedding route prewarm path performed an idempotent cache rewrite that re-registered old variant mapping for embeddings.create binding due to non-atomic update ordering.

Race vector: non-atomic route update + asynchronous prewarm acknowledgement + per-route sticky-affinity table updated independently for different route namespaces (chat vs embeddings). Affinity token is global but per-route sticky mapping applied in separate codepaths.
Observed that forcing a TTL bump on affinity tokens temporarily reduced occurrence (likely because it forced refreshes and re-resolution to current mapping).
Related: SUP-302118 noted similar session divergence when health probes overlapped with rollout windows; recommend cross-checking prior mitigation history.
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigation accepted by customer (explicit pin to same variant across chat+embed). Engineering to merge atomic-commit patch to canary-coordinator and edge-proxy that serializes route updates across co-located route groups. Patch will also add a 250ms quiesce window where prewarm cache writes are deferred until commit completes. Plan: ship hotfix to staging 2026-03-13, promote to prod us-east 2026-03-14 during low-traffic window. Post-deploy: monitor mismatch rate and rollback if >0.5% within 30 minutes.
follow_up_actions: Merge PRs and schedule hotfix deploy: edge-proxy PR 4392, canary-coordinator PR 1187
Add automated unit/integration test that simulates concurrent canary commit + prewarm and asserts strong consistency across multiple routes for same affinity token
Update runbook: add 'quiesce prewarm on commit' step and include diagnostic query for mixed-variant traces
Coordinate with BrightDocs to remove temporary pin after validation window and collect 48h of telemetry
